name: Maximum-to-minimum distance ratio
description: Place 16 distinct points in two-dimensional Euclidean space to minimize the squared ratio of maximum to minimum pairwise distance.
limitations: Paper reports over 50 mathematical problems but explicitly details 13 families in Appendix B. Unpublished full task inventory and internal Google assets prevent a complete runnable reproduction.

Official result notebook provides mathematical constructions and verification, but no AlphaEvolve search implementation. It publishes a subset of all evaluated problems; the full >50 mathematical problem inventory is not disclosed.

Paper Appendix B.3 writes max(abs(autoconvolution)); notebook B.3 reported 1.4557 construction computes abs(max(autoconvolution)). The notebook separately verifies the max(abs(...)) variant at 1.4688. These are not interchangeable metrics.
Execution interface inspected in pinned source. Full paper experiments have not been reproduced here.

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
